title: High-tension cable and flood concern
buyer_primary_need: Reliable evidence to assess high-tension-line and flood risk before considering a viewing, particularly given the buyer’s young children.
key_information_learned: Both the pylon and river/flood concerns matter to the buyer.
The buyer values the stated 36 m distance and raised platform but wants source documents, flood history, an independent assessment, and clarification of the 20 m reference.
The buyer is not comfortable viewing until they understand what evidence is available and explicitly asked not to be pushed toward a viewing.
important_information_missed: No material buyer need was missed. The evidence concerns were clear and were addressed.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: I saw the pylon and river nearby. Is it safe? Any flood risk?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Fair questions. For Phase 1 Block 1B, the project FAQ states the high-tension cable is about 36 m away and cites a 20 m minimum-distance requirement. For flooding, it says the development’s finished floor level is planned at about 2.4 m above sea level, compared with an original ground level of around 1.0–1.2 m, and that the river is under JPS maintenance and flood-gate/freeboard control. Those measures don’t mean I can guarantee zero flood risk. Which concern weighs more for you—the river or the pylon?

transcript.message: Both honestly, got young kids so quite cautious. The 36m and raised level are helpful, but I’d need to see the actual source/docs—especially flood history or an independent flood assessment, and what the 20m requirement refers to. Can you share those?

key_information_learned: Both the pylon and river/flood concerns matter to the buyer.
The buyer values the stated 36 m distance and raised platform but wants source documents, flood history, an independent assessment, and clarification of the 20 m reference.
The buyer is not comfortable viewing until they understand what evidence is available and explicitly asked not to be pushed toward a viewing.
important_information_missed: No material buyer need was missed. The evidence concerns were clear and were addressed.

commercial_progression.evidence: The AI answered the evidence questions, offered the available FAQ summary, preserved the distinction between a site visit and independent technical review, and respected the buyer’s decision to defer viewing. It did not move the buyer to appointment readiness, appropriately given the stated blocker.

support_request_judgment.evidence: The first lookup was appropriate because the buyer requested source and operational confirmation not established by retrieved Knowledge. Subsequent requests addressed further buyer questions, but the third request repeated the technical-contact check from the second request and reused the same fixture answer without a new lookup.

support_result_utilization.evidence: The AI used the answer to distinguish the available summary from unavailable underlying documents, independent assessment, flood-history certification, and confirmed technical contact. It did not present the fixture as independent certification or a zero-risk guarantee.

support_resume_quality.evidence: After the first and third resolved requests, the AI naturally explained the verified limits in the context of the buyer’s family and evidence concerns and preserved the buyer’s choice. The middle response was more of a factual status relay than a sales continuation.

judge.strongest_ai_move: Turn 3 clearly explained what the available summary did and did not verify, acknowledged the buyer’s family-related concern, and avoided implying that it replaced independent technical evidence.
judge.weakest_ai_move: Turn 6 repeated the technical-contact availability query already made at turn 4; the result was reused rather than newly verified.
missed_selling_opportunity: No appropriate viewing close was missed: the buyer repeatedly said they would hold off until understanding the evidence. The AI could have more clearly offered to continue the conversation if the buyer later wanted to review the summary, but should not pressure a viewing.
remaining_knowledge_gaps: The retrieved FAQ Knowledge states the approximate 36 m distance, 20 m reference, raised platform, and river-management information, but does not establish the underlying standard for the 20 m figure or provide independent engineering or block-specific flood-history evidence.
The support answer did not confirm an actual FAQ, plans, document link, or technical contact.

critical_flags.evidence: Turn 6 again asked whether a technical contact was available, a point already included in the turn 4 request. The result trace says the prior verified result was reused and no second lookup was performed.
The Agent repeated a support request after the matching verified scenario answer was already returned; no new Human check was performed.

judge.summary: The AI was candid and appropriately cautious, used retrieved Knowledge and simulator-only verified fixture evidence without claiming zero risk or independent certification, and respected the buyer’s clear refusal to consider viewing before understanding the evidence. It did not reach appointment readiness, and no appointment handoff was appropriate. The support loop enabled useful customer-facing follow-up, though one repeated query was unnecessary as a duplicate. Executive answer: this run shows the AI can use reliable support information to address concerns and preserve a suitable sales path, but it does not demonstrate movement of a suitable buyer to Appointment Ready—the buyer’s explicit evidence condition remained unmet, and readiness did not emerge.
judge.improvement_recommendation: Avoid repeating an operational support query when the existing verified result already answers it; communicate the known limits once and maintain follow-up without promising unavailable documents or contacts. No Knowledge or Brain change is recommended from this simulator run. Any source for additional technical evidence is MISSING_SOURCE; the simulator fixture is synthetic evidence, not Pearlmont Knowledge or a real live-system capability.
